chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: George Brown's Watts nightclub and the dating of Jelly Roll's story
summary: George Brown was a political fixer who ran a small club in Watts; Jelly Roll's Cadillac story dates to 1917, before Spikes built the Wayside Inn in 1922.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x:
Ohhhh, that's interesting. And he said that the
place in Watts was owned by George Brown. Who's George Brown?

Well, George Brown had a... He's all mixed up.
George Brown had a nightclub. I told you I played out there for Rudolph
Valentino. Well, you see, you couldn't buy liquor in Los Angeles but you
could buy it in Watts, so George Brown was a big politician--a fixer, you
know. Anything you got in jail or anything, he could fix it fer you. So
he had a little dump out there. All colored people went to it but...
but Jelly Roll might've played there, I don't know, but over where we
played was two blocks from there was Baron Long's, and it was all...
'course I don't know whether he barred colored people or not. I never
saw any in there. But all the big movie stars and all the big actors and
all the big millionaires came there, you know...where we played. But
George Brown had a dump down two, three blocks from us.

But when Jelly Roll left the Cadillac and went
to Watts, he went to the Wayside Inn--he went to your place. Right?

No. No, it wasn't built then. He...I built the
Wayside Inn in about '22 but what he's talkin' about is uh...uh, around
'15 or '17, ain't he?

There's no date in here. It just says "When he
first came to Los Angeles..." Oh, yeah, I beg your pardon: '17, I'm sorry.
